# `Q-16-5` — Shortcode value not found

> A `meta`, `var`, or `env` shortcode could not resolve its key; the
> invocation renders as a visible `?name` marker.

## What this means

Three built-in shortcodes look a value up somewhere and substitute it
into the document:

| Shortcode          | Reads from                        |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `{{{< meta key >}}}` | the document's merged metadata    |
| `{{{< var key >}}}`  | `_variables.yml`                  |
| `{{{< env NAME >}}}` | the process environment           |

The handler was found and ran — the failure is that the key it was
asked for does not exist. Since there is no value to substitute,
Quarto renders a visible `?name` marker in its place rather than an
empty gap, so a missing value is obvious in the output instead of
silently reading as a typo or a missing word.

## Why this happens

- **A typo in the key.**
- **The key is defined at a different level than you expect.** `meta`
  reads *merged* metadata — front matter plus `_quarto.yml` plus any
  active profile overlay. A key defined only in a profile that is not
  active resolves to nothing.
- **`_variables.yml` is missing or in the wrong place.** It belongs at
  the project root, next to `_quarto.yml`.
- **A dotted path into a value that is not a mapping.**
  `{{{< meta author.name >}}}` needs `author` to be a mapping with a
  `name` key; if `author` is a plain string, the path resolves to
  nothing.
- **An environment variable not set in the rendering process.** A
  variable set in your interactive shell is not necessarily present
  in the environment that runs Quarto, particularly under an editor or
  CI.

## How to fix

Define the key at the source the shortcode reads from.

For `meta`, in the front matter or `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
---
version: "2.1"
---

Version {{{< meta version >}}}.
```

For `var`, in `_variables.yml` at the project root:

```yaml
product:
  name: Quarto
```

```markdown
{{{< var product.name >}}}
```

For `env`, give a fallback so an unset variable is not a failure:

```markdown
{{{< env BUILD_ID local >}}}
```

The fallback is the second argument; with it, an unset `BUILD_ID`
renders as `local` and no warning is emitted. This is the right shape
for anything that is set in CI but not on a developer machine.
